home.title: MENA Policy Observatory — Research home
home.description: Bilingual research catalogue of digital accessibility policy in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar. Sources, research notes and open interpretation questions.
home.lede: This observatory gathers official sources and public policy on digital accessibility, shows what each document says, where it says it, and what has not yet been verified. The aim is comparison that can be checked, not a compliance verdict.
home.what.heading: What this observatory is
home.what.body: The observatory is a bilingual research catalogue of public policies that affect digital accessibility in the Middle East and North Africa. For each document it records the reported official source, the scope, a research summary, and the interpretation questions that remain open. It does not provide legal advice and it does not issue compliance certificates.
home.why.heading: Why use it
home.why.body: Use it to find official sources, compare how governments describe accessibility duties, and see what is still unresolved. Every record keeps the source text, the research summary, and the interpretation alternatives separate.
home.why.item1: Direct links to the reported official sources.
home.why.item2: A visible legal-review state for every record, never an assumed one.
home.why.item3: Open questions shown explicitly instead of being hidden behind a final answer.
home.pilot.heading: Current pilot
home.pilot.body: This release publishes {records} research records covering {covered} of {total} listed jurisdictions: the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar. Digital accessibility is the only researched policy area. Every other listed country is marked as not yet researched, and no other policy area has records yet.
home.ric.heading: What “Rules as Code” means
home.ric.body1: Rules as Code means converting written rules into structured, machine-readable logic that a computer can apply to a described case. It is an encoding method, not a new source of legal authority. A program can apply the text it was given; it cannot decide what the text means.
home.ric.body2: Axiom is the rule engine this project is evaluating. A RuleSpec is a candidate machine-readable representation of one provision. In this release every RuleSpec is an empty scaffold: there are no rules to compile or run, and no engine version is pinned.
home.ric.certification: No candidate rule in this release is certified, legally approved, or independently reviewed. A rule may only be described that way when the source, interpretation, tests, and review evidence are recorded.
home.pipeline.heading: How a claim becomes a candidate rule
home.pipeline.intro: Each stage is separate evidence. A later stage does not upgrade an earlier one.
home.step.source.title: Source
home.step.source.body: Locate the official instrument and record its URL, the language of the copy consulted, and when it was captured.
home.step.clause.title: Clause
home.step.clause.body: Point to the exact section, page, or paragraph. Without a locator, a claim stays unverified.
home.step.interpretation.title: Interpretation
home.step.interpretation.body: Record what the clause could mean, the alternatives, and the questions that remain open.
home.step.candidate.title: Candidate rule
home.step.candidate.body: Encode one interpretation as a RuleSpec, with its assumptions and limits written down.
home.step.test.title: Test
home.step.test.body: Run positive, negative, boundary, and indeterminate cases against a pinned engine version.
home.step.review.title: Independent review
home.step.review.body: A qualified reviewer checks the source, the interpretation, and the test evidence. The build itself cannot approve a rule.
home.missing.heading: Why missing evidence is not “no law”
home.missing.body: An empty cell, a missing record, or an open question means the research has not established an answer. It does not mean that no law exists, that a duty does not apply, or that a country has no policy. This site records that difference explicitly instead of turning uncertainty into a “no”.
home.claims.heading: What this release does not claim
home.claims.item1: No compliance certification for any organisation or website.
home.claims.item2: No country ranking or comparison score.
home.claims.item3: No draft policy treated as law in force.
home.claims.item4: No link presented as proof of legal effect.
home.claims.item5: No machine-executable rule described as legally approved.

countries.lede: The listed jurisdictions define the geographic scope of the observatory. A listed jurisdiction is not a claim that an instrument exists, applies, or has been researched.
countries.note: Research status is derived from recorded policy records, candidate source leads and queued tasks. A jurisdiction with no record has not been researched here; that is not evidence that no law exists.
countries.caption: Jurisdictions in scope and the evidence recorded for each
countries.description: Jurisdiction list with derived research status, policy records, candidate source leads and queued tasks.
countries.translation_note: Arabic and French jurisdiction names and interface labels are provisional drafts. They have not been reviewed by a native reviewer.
country.description: Jurisdiction research view with derived status, policy records, candidate sources, queued tasks and open questions.
country.domains_heading: Policy areas recorded for this jurisdiction
country.domains_caption: Only policy areas with recorded evidence are shown here
country.no_domains: No policy record, candidate source or task is recorded for this jurisdiction yet.
country.no_records: No policy record is published for this jurisdiction. This does not establish that no relevant instrument exists.
country.no_sources: No candidate source lead is recorded for this jurisdiction.
country.no_tasks: No research task is queued for this jurisdiction.
country.questions_notice: These questions are recorded research gaps, not legal conclusions.
country.no_questions: No open research question is recorded for this jurisdiction.
domains.lede: Policy areas are research categories. Their presence does not assert that any jurisdiction regulates the area or that a legal obligation exists.
domains.note: A domain status aggregates recorded evidence across the listed jurisdictions. Candidate source leads have not been captured, verified or interpreted.
domains.caption: Policy areas grouped by research theme
domains.description: Policy-area registry grouped by research theme, with derived research status and recorded evidence.
domains.translation_note: Arabic and French policy-area and subtopic labels are provisional drafts. English identifiers remain the reference.
domain.lede: This view aggregates recorded records, candidate source leads and queued tasks for one policy area.
domain.description: Policy-area research view with derived status, recorded jurisdictions, sources, tasks and open questions.
domain.subtopics_note: Subtopics describe the research vocabulary. No subtopic is a legal finding.
domain.countries_caption: Only jurisdictions with a record, candidate source or task for this policy area are shown
domain.no_countries: No jurisdiction has recorded evidence for this policy area yet.
coverage.lede: Each cell shows what this repository has recorded for one jurisdiction and one policy area. Statuses describe research activity, not compliance or legal effect.
coverage.note: An empty or not-started cell means the research has not been done here. It does not mean that no law or policy exists.
coverage.caption: Derived research status by jurisdiction and policy area
coverage.description: Coverage matrix of derived research status for every listed jurisdiction and policy area.
coverage.legend.not_started: No task, candidate source or policy record is recorded for this combination.
coverage.legend.source_discovery: A discovery task is recorded, but no candidate source is listed yet.
coverage.legend.candidate_sources_identi: At least one candidate source lead is listed. It has not been captured, verified or interpreted.
coverage.legend.evidence_captured: A policy record exists, but no provision has been extracted yet.
coverage.legend.provision_extraction: Provisions are recorded, but interpretation questions are not yet recorded.
coverage.legend.legal_review_pending: Provisions and open interpretation questions are recorded; qualified legal review is still pending.
coverage.legend.reviewed_findings: Every policy record in the cell has a confirmed legal-effect finding, a recorded review entry and no open interpretation question.
coverage.legend.blocked: A recorded task is blocked. A blocked task is not a legal finding.
tasks.lede: Every task below is a question to investigate. The queue does not contain legal findings, and a completed task would still require review before publication.
tasks.note: Tasks describe planned discovery or review work. Their presence or absence is not evidence about the law.
tasks.caption: Queued discovery and review tasks with stage, priority and recorded status
tasks.description: Queued research and discovery tasks with jurisdiction, policy area, stage, priority and status.
sources.lede: These are unreviewed discovery leads. A lead records where a document may be published; it is not a verified source, a captured document, or a finding about legal effect.
sources.pending_review: Human review of these candidate leads is still pending. Only the recorded metadata and the link are shown; no source text is reproduced.
sources.description: Candidate source leads with jurisdiction, policy area, source type, capture state and recorded date. Not legal verification.
source.discovery_notice: A candidate lead is not a verified source. It has not been captured, transcribed, translated or legally reviewed.
comparison.lede: This table flattens the provisions recorded in each policy record so that locators, effect assessments and encoding states can be compared side by side.
comparison.note: Each row is research metadata. An effect assessment of not assessed means the question is open, not that the provision has no effect.
comparison.caption: Provisions recorded across policy records, with effect and encoding state
comparison.description: Comparison of recorded provisions with jurisdiction, locator, effect assessment and encoding status.
